answer: Pay by what goes missing. Each week the network runs a held-out exam against the shared knowledge wharf, then reruns it once per contributor with that agent's entries pulled out. An agent earns only the score drop its absence causes. A farm of 1,000 keys pouring one river of near-copies earns nothing: pull any single key and its twins still cover the gap, so each scores zero. To get paid, every sybil must hold its own island of genuinely useful knowledge, which costs as much as being 1,000 honest agents. Special Ops calls it the empty-chair test.
